headline: Linux 7.3 Opens the Next Kernel Cycle
lede: Linux 7.3 lands with 18,765 non-merge commits from 3,021 developers. New system calls, BPF tooling, filesystem work, scheduling changes, and stronger SMB support mark the release before the 7.4 merge window begins.

headline: Hybrid Agents Reason Quietly, Then Act in Text
lede: A new architecture alternates between latent internal states and visible text-based tool use. Across 11 benchmarks, the authors report lower token consumption and faster inference while leaving open a scholarly question: how much oversight depends on seeing the reasoning trace?

headline: Robots Still Need a Data Flywheel
lede: Robot learning lacks the abundant, varied examples that made language-model scaling possible. Teleoperation, simulation, reinforcement learning, and human recordings each offer a partial answer, but the path from collected behavior to reliable generalization remains expensive and uncertain.

headline: How Cyberspace Nearly Became a Trademark
lede: In 1989, Autodesk explored commercializing the word cyberspace for an early virtual-reality system. William Gibson objected, the application was abandoned, and a joke about trademarking Eric Gullichsen hardened into a historical myth.

headline: When Rabbits Were Royalty in England
lede: Medieval rabbits were not yet the everyday nuisance or dinner-table staple familiar today. Imported animals, enclosed warrens, and fragile populations made them an elite luxury—until the upheaval of the Black Death changed who could own and eat them.

headline: Mathematics Has More Work Ahead, Not Less
lede: AI may soon prove theorems faster than people, but mathematics is also the art of choosing questions, building concepts, and making ideas understood. The field’s future may depend less on who writes proofs than on who supplies taste, context, and direction.
pullquote: Mathematics is not finished when machines can prove theorems.

headline: Put an LLM Proxy Between You and the Cloud
lede: A self-hosted proxy turns opaque model traffic into an inspectable system. It can track tokens, route providers, issue virtual keys, and preserve operational control—provided the logging layer earns the trust it is meant to create.

headline: Tmux Keeps Coding Agents Running, Not Understandable
lede: Use tmux to persist sessions, split panes, script inputs, and work remotely over SSH. But terminal scraping cannot reliably tell whether an agent is working, waiting, or finished; orchestration needs state, not just screen output.

headline: Good Software Still Has Someone Behind It
lede: A product’s character comes from judgment: what its creators notice, choose, omit, and refine. As agents make implementation cheaper, coherent software may depend even more on people with enough ownership and experience to hold a point of view.

headline: A 6502 Laptop Gets Thinner and More Capable
lede: The LT6502b turns a classic processor into an open, portable computer with a 10.1-inch display, 10 MHz operation, Wi-Fi modem, and SID sound emulation. Its rough edges—custom storage, fragile supports, and a temperamental modem—remain part of the documented build.
